steps.title: Prepare Homogenization Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the lysis buffer mix and ensure all materials are ready.

substeps.instruction: Warm the 'Vesterinen' lysis buffer [0.4M NaCl, 10mM Tris-HCl, 2mM EDTA, 2% SDS] in warm water to dissolve any precipitate.

Prepare a mix of lysis buffer and Proteinase K (stored at -20°C). For 100 standard samples, mix 19,500 μL of lysis buffer and 500 μL of Proteinase K (standard per-sample ratio: 195 μL buffer to 5 μL Proteinase K).

steps.title: Set Up Homogenization Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare 91 screw-cap tubes (2 ml) for 88 insects and 3 negative control extraction blanks (3C, 6C, 9C).

substeps.instruction: Label the side of the tubes with sample IDs.
Place tubes on a 96-well rack, keeping caps on aluminum foil to avoid contamination.
Add 200 μL of the prepared buffer mix to each tube (use more than 200 μL for larger insects).
Add one 2.8mm bead and one small spoon of 0.5mm beads (sterilize the spoon with a flame before use). For larger insects, add 2-3 big beads.

steps.title: Add Specimens to Tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer insect specimens into the prepared tubes while maintaining sterility.

substeps.instruction: Place each insect on a paper towel first to remove external ethanol.
Transfer specimens using tweezers, sterilizing tweezers with a flame between every individual or eppendorf.
For very large insects (e.g., bees), cut into smaller pieces and divide into two 2 ml screw-cap tubes; sterilize the scalpel/tweezers after each sample.
Close the tubes immediately after adding the specimen.
Record sample metadata (trap ID, size, buffer volume, Order/Group/species, sex) on the homogenization sheet.

steps.title: Homogenize and Incubate
steps.instruction: Mechanically disrupt the samples and incubate to lyse cells.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes in a homogenizer (e.g., Bead Ruptor Elite) and grind two times for 30 s at 5m/s speed.
Incubate samples in a thermal block or water bath at 55°C for 2 hours.
Vortex samples 1-2 times during the incubation period.
Cool samples to room temperature before proceeding to DNA extraction or storage (fridge/freezer). For bees split into two tubes, combine the contents after incubation and vortex.

steps.title: Prepare PCR I Primers
steps.instruction: Create primer mixes from 100μM stock primers.

substeps.instruction: Prepare separate forward and reverse mixes. Each mix must contain: COI [2.5μM], 16S V4 [10μM], and 16S V1-2 [5μM].
Distribute primer mix aliquots into strip tubes: MA_P5 - MH_P5, M1_P7 - M8_P7, and M9_P7 - M12_P7 to facilitate multi-channel pipetting.

steps.title: Verify PCR 1 Products
steps.instruction: Perform electrophoresis to check PCR 1 success.

substeps.instruction: Run a subset of PCR 1 products on a 2.5% agarose gel using 2 μL PCR product and 2 μL loading dye.
Ensure all negative and positive controls are included on the gel.

steps.title: Clean PCR 1 Products
steps.instruction: Purify PCR 1 products using SPRI Beads.

substeps.instruction: Prepare fresh 80% EtOH aliquots.
Transfer 8-10 μL of PCR 1 product per sample to a 96 deep-well plate.
Add 20 μL of SPRI Beads and mix by pipetting or plate shaker.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Place on a magnetic stand for 2 min and remove supernatant with a multichannel pipette.
Wash beads twice: add 100 μL of 80% EtOH to each well, incubate on magnetic stand for 1 min, and remove supernatant.
Wait up to 4 min on the magnetic stand until the bead pellet is dry.
Add 20 μL of TE buffer, mix, and incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Place on magnetic stand for 2 min and transfer 20 μL of supernatant to a new 96-well plate.
Store plate at 4°C (short term) or -20°C (long term).

steps.title: Verify PCR 2 Products
steps.instruction: Run PCR 2 products on a 2.5% agarose gel (2 μL PCR product + 2 μL loading dye).

steps.title: Pool Libraries
steps.instruction: Create a library pool from each 96-well plate based on gel band intensity.

substeps.instruction: Mix PCR 2 products in a 1.5 mL microtube using the following volumes: Very strong band (0.5 μL), Strong band (1 μL), Medium band (2 μL), Weak band (4 μL), No visible band (8 μL).

steps.title: Clean Plate Pools
steps.instruction: Purify the plate pools using the Promega ProNex® Size-Selective Purification System.

substeps.instruction: Use a 1/1.5 (v/v) pool to magnetic beads ratio (standard volume: 80 μL of pool).

steps.title: Quantify Plate Pools
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentrations of plate pools using a Qubit Fluorometer with 1X dsDNA High Sensitivity (HS) or Broad Range (BR) Assay Kits.

steps.title: Create Master Pool
steps.instruction: Combine plate pools into a single Master Pool.

substeps.instruction: Mix plate pools based on sample number and DNA concentration.
Adjust mixing ratios if plate pools differ in target gene composition (e.g., COI only vs. all three target genes).

steps.title: Clean Master Pool
steps.instruction: Purify the Master Pool using the Promega ProNex® system.

substeps.instruction: Use a 1/1.3 (v/v) pool to magnetic beads ratio.
Suspend the final product in TE x 0.1 or ddH2O to the desired DNA concentration.

steps.title: Final Quantification and Quality Check
steps.instruction: Perform final quality control on the Master Pool.

substeps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration using Qubit 1X dsDNA HS or BR Assay Kits.
Check for primer-dimers using a Bioanalyzer or Tapestation.
If primer-dimers are detected, repeat the Master Pool cleaning step.

description: Overview For amplicon library preparation we use a two-step PCR approach. During the first step (PCR1) we amplify three target genes: COI, 16S V1-2 region and 16S V4 region, in multiplex reaction. Next we clean PCR1 products with magnetic beads. Finally, during the second step (PCR2) we add the indexes and illumina adapters to the amplified sequences. Two-step PCR overview Protocol overview, general instructions, and considerations Quantitative Multi-Target Amplicon Sequencing is an approach originally developed for the characterization of microbiota in large collections of diverse insects. It enables the molecular identification of the host insects and the characterization of the abundance and genotype- and clade-level diversity and distribution of their associated bacteria. This is achieved through simultaneous amplification of insect (COI) and bacterial (16S rRNA) marker genes, the latter in a quantitative manner, and the preparation of Illumina-compatible sequencing libraries in a highly multiplexed manner. This protocol has been initially developed and optimized for the cost-effective preparation of large numbers of amplicon sequencing libraries for these two target regions. However, it can be easily adapted to incorporate other marker regions for different organisms potentially present in samples, or adapted for other types of biological samples. Parts of the protocol can be executed on their own and combined with other methods. Many of the solutions implemented in the protocol, including quantification of targets or use of "phased" primers, are optional. The protocol presented here starts with a set of 88 diverse ethanol-preserved insects selected from a Malaise trap. This number, alongside different positive and negative controls, is sufficient to fill a 96-well plate.
